title: Run-Time Loading with LoadLibrary and GetProcAddress
summary: Instead of linking against an import library, a program can load a DLL whenever it likes with `LoadLibraryW`, look up functions by name with `GetProcAddress`, call them through function pointers, and unload the DLL with `FreeLibrary`. This is the foundation of plugins and hot reload.
markdown:
## Three functions

```cpp-norun
HMODULE LoadLibraryW(LPCWSTR fileName);                 // map the DLL (and its dependencies); NULL on failure
FARPROC GetProcAddress(HMODULE module, LPCSTR name);    // address of an export; NULL if not found
BOOL    FreeLibrary(HMODULE module);                     // drop one reference; unmap at zero
```

`HMODULE` is a handle to a loaded module. Its value is in fact the module's base address. Note that `GetProcAddress` takes an **ANSI** string (there is no `W` version), because export names are plain bytes.

## A complete example

StoneMath from lesson 1.03, now with `extern "C"` exports (lesson 2.01). The program does **not** link `StoneMath.lib` and does not include its header:

```cpp-norun
#include <windows.h>
#include <iostream>

using StackHeightFn = int (*)(int, int);           // must match the DLL's declaration exactly

int main()
{
    HMODULE dll{ LoadLibraryW(L"StoneMath.dll") };
    if (!dll)
    {
        std::cerr << "Could not load StoneMath.dll, error " << GetLastError() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }

    auto stackHeight{ reinterpret_cast<StackHeightFn>(GetProcAddress(dll, "stackHeight")) };
    if (!stackHeight)
    {
        std::cerr << "StoneMath.dll has no stackHeight\n";
        FreeLibrary(dll);
        return 1;
    }

    std::cout << stackHeight(10, 4) << '\n';     // 3
    FreeLibrary(dll);
}
```

The `reinterpret_cast` is needed because `GetProcAddress` returns a generic `FARPROC`. The compiler cannot check that the type you cast to is right: if the DLL's function takes `(double, int)` and you cast to `int(*)(int, int)`, the call compiles and silently passes garbage. Keep function pointer types in a header shared with the DLL.

> [!note] Why not just link?
> Run-time loading lets the program start even when the DLL is missing, choose which DLL to load (say, `renderer_d3d11.dll` or `renderer_vulkan.dll`), load DLLs it has never heard of (plugins), and unload and reload a DLL (hot reload).

## Errors

When `LoadLibraryW` returns `NULL`, `GetLastError()` says why:

| Code | Name | Usual cause |
|---|---|---|
| 126 | `ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND` | The DLL, **or one of its dependencies**, was not found |
| 127 | `ERROR_PROC_NOT_FOUND` | A dependency is missing an export the DLL imports |
| 193 | `ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT` | 32-bit DLL in a 64-bit process, or not a DLL at all |
| 1114 | `ERROR_DLL_INIT_FAILED` | The DLL's `DllMain` returned `FALSE` |

Error 126 is confusing: the DLL you named may be right there, but something *it* needs is not. Lesson 1.06's tools find out which.

## Reference counting

Each successful `LoadLibraryW` of the same DLL increases its reference count and returns the **same** `HMODULE`. Each `FreeLibrary` decreases it. The DLL is unmapped only when the count reaches zero.

```cpp-norun
HMODULE a{ LoadLibraryW(L"StoneMath.dll") };   // count 1, maps the DLL
HMODULE b{ LoadLibraryW(L"StoneMath.dll") };   // count 2, a == b
FreeLibrary(a);                                // count 1, still mapped
FreeLibrary(b);                                // count 0, unmapped
```

After the last `FreeLibrary`, every function pointer you got from that DLL points at memory that no longer belongs to it. Calling one crashes. So does using any object, string or vtable the DLL created. Lesson 5.03 deals with this carefully.

## A small RAII wrapper

Forgetting `FreeLibrary` on an error path is easy. Wrap the handle:

```cpp-norun
class Library
{
public:
    explicit Library(const wchar_t* file) : m_module{ LoadLibraryW(file) } {}
    ~Library() { if (m_module) FreeLibrary(m_module); }
    Library(const Library&) = delete;
    Library& operator=(const Library&) = delete;

    explicit operator bool() const { return m_module != nullptr; }

    template <typename Fn>
    Fn get(const char* name) const { return reinterpret_cast<Fn>(GetProcAddress(m_module, name)); }

private:
    HMODULE m_module;
};
```

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Casting to the wrong function type
> The compiler cannot catch it. Share the typedef with the DLL.

> [!warning] Calling a function after FreeLibrary
> Pointers into an unloaded DLL are dangling. Drop them before you free the library.

> [!warning] Passing a relative name and getting the wrong file
> `LoadLibraryW(L"StoneMath.dll")` searches several folders. Lesson 4.02 shows how to load exactly the file you mean.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? What do LoadLibraryW, GetProcAddress and FreeLibrary each do?
- Load a DLL's import library; call an exported function by name; delete the DLL file
+ Map a DLL and return its handle; look up an exported function's address by name; drop one reference and unmap the DLL when none remain
- Map a DLL and call its exports; return a typed function pointer; unmap the DLL immediately
> `GetProcAddress` only returns an untyped address, and `FreeLibrary` unmaps the DLL only when its reference count reaches zero.

? What happens to function pointers from a DLL after its last FreeLibrary?
- They keep working, because the code stays in the process until it exits
- They become null automatically
+ They dangle: the code they point to is no longer mapped, so calling them crashes
> Nothing resets your pointers. Drop them before the last `FreeLibrary`.

? Which of these does run-time loading make possible that load-time linking does not?
+ Starting without the DLL and choosing between several DLLs while running
- Calling the DLL's functions without any function pointer
- Using the DLL's exports without them being in its export table
> Run-time loading also allows plugins found at run time and unloading and reloading code. `GetProcAddress` can still only find exported names.

? LoadLibraryW fails with error 126, but StoneMath.dll is next to the program. What is the most likely cause?
- The file is too large
+ One of StoneMath.dll's own dependencies is missing
- GetProcAddress was called first
- StoneMath.dll is 32-bit and the program is 64-bit
> 126 means "module not found", and it covers every module the loader needs. A wrong architecture gives 193 instead.

? A DLL is loaded twice and freed once. Is it still mapped?
- No; one FreeLibrary always unmaps it
- Only in Debug builds
+ Yes; its reference count is still 1
> Each LoadLibrary is matched by one FreeLibrary.

? Why must the function pointer type match the DLL's function exactly?
+ The address is untyped, so a wrong cast breaks the call silently
- Otherwise GetProcAddress returns NULL for that name
- The DLL checks the caller's type and refuses the call
> `GetProcAddress` looks up a name only; the type exists only in your cast, so a mismatch passes arguments the wrong way with no compiler error.
```
ideas:
- Load StoneMath at run time as above. Then rename the DLL and check the error code.
- Print the `HMODULE` value and compare it with the base address in the Modules window.
- Write a program that loads `renderer_a.dll` or `renderer_b.dll` depending on a command-line argument, both exporting `const char* rendererName()`.
